chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about prayer on a ship. He said, 'If it is heavily laden and when you stand in it it does not move, then pray standing. And if it is light and tilts, then pray sitting.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer on a ship according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-mashiqqa* (hardship) in maritime jurisprudence, prioritizing physical stability over the standard posture of standing. It reflects the practical legal reasoning of the Imams, who adapted ritual obligations to the variable conditions of 8th-century sea travel, ensuring the validity of prayer without compromising the worshipper's balance.
